heading: 4.1 Objective One: MAS alone and MAS combined with hs-CRP
objective: To compare the diagnostic accuracy of MAS alone with the both-positive and either-positive MAS–hs-CRP strategies in suspected acute appendicitis. hs-CRP alone is retained as the component-test comparator.
methods: Histopathology was the reference standard: acute, suppurative, phlegmonous, gangrenous and perforated appendicitis were positive; reactive lymphoid hyperplasia was negative. Simple appendicitis comprised the first three positive categories and complicated appendicitis comprised gangrenous or perforated disease. MAS ≥7 and hs-CRP >3 mg/L were positive. “MAS and hs-CRP” required both tests to be positive; “MAS or hs-CRP” required either test to be positive. Neither combination was designated the single prespecified primary rule. All four strategies used the same 85 complete operated-patient records, including 77 reference-positive and eight reference-negative patients. This selected cohort may not represent all patients with suspected appendicitis. Proportion intervals use the Wilson method; likelihood-ratio intervals use the approximate log method. Paired binary comparisons use exact McNemar tests with Holm adjustment across nine tests. Raw-score AUC intervals use 1,000 stratified bootstrap resamples, and correlated AUCs are compared by DeLong’s method.
finalParagraph: Combining MAS and hs-CRP changes the balance between missed appendicitis and false-positive classifications. The either-positive strategy had higher observed sensitivity, whereas the both-positive strategy had higher observed specificity. Adjusted paired tests did not establish superiority, and the limited negative-reference sample prevents firm clinical recommendations.
